title: Let's Encrypt TLS Challenge failing when behind a Traefik TCP Router
body: I have one public IP forwarding ports 80 and 443 to Server 1. Server 1 uses HostSNIRegexp TCP routers with TLS passthrough and PROXY protocol v2 to send traffic to Traefik instances on Servers 2 and 3. Those downstream instances use Let's Encrypt TLS challenges. Certificate requests behind Server 1 fail with HTTP 400, while certificate requests handled directly by Server 1 work. This affects all requested domains, not only names with a www prefix. I am using Traefik 3.0.0 on linux/amd64. The behavior started with 3.0.0-rc4; downgrading the gateway to 3.0.0-rc3 makes it work again.

symptoms_visible: When Server 1 forwards TLS by SNI to Servers 2 or 3, their Let's Encrypt TLS certificate requests fail with error 400.
Certificate requests handled directly on Server 1 work.
The failures occur on 3.0.0 and started with 3.0.0-rc4; after downgrading the gateway to 3.0.0-rc3, certificate issuance works again.
N0.label: N0 downstream TLS challenges fail after gateway regression

symptoms_visible: Downstream TLS challenges fail on the affected gateway versions even though ordinary SNI-based TLS passthrough routes reach the downstream servers.
N1.label: N1 ACME challenge interception identified

symptoms_visible: My gateway needs its own ACME resolver for some routes while forwarding other TLS routes to downstream systems that obtain their own certificates.
N2_x.label: N2_x resolver-removal direction rejected by deployment requirement

symptoms_visible: I tested the developer branch and TLS passthrough is working again.
N3.label: N3 candidate behavior verified by affected user

symptoms_visible: With ACME bypass allowed on the TLS entry point, ACME TLS traffic follows the matching passthrough router and reaches the downstream service.
N_terminal.label: terminal ACME passthrough restored

solution.intent: Identify the regression as Traefik's new interception of ACME TLS-ALPN challenges before normal TCP passthrough routing, rather than a downstream certificate or SNI configuration failure.
solution.concrete_example: The affected gateway versions detect the ACME TLS challenge and send it to the gateway's internal ACME handling before the HostSNI passthrough router can forward it. That explains why direct gateway issuance works, downstream issuance fails, and the older release works.
solution.inference_hint: Maintainers mapped the reporter's rc3/rc4 boundary to a security-motivated behavior change. The conclusion that the gateway's internal ACME handler preempts normal TCP router selection is engineer-side diagnosis, not wording supplied by the reporter.

edges.comment: Maintainer diagnosis from c4 and c7-c8: the rc4-era security change intentionally intercepted ACME TLS challenges even when a matching TCP router used TLS passthrough.

solution.intent: Avoid interception by removing the TLS challenge resolver from the gateway and only permit downstream challenge passthrough when no gateway TLS resolver is configured.
solution.concrete_example: Run the internet-facing gateway without a TLS challenge resolver so ACME TLS traffic can be handled by the custom passthrough routers instead of the gateway's internal ACME handler.

edges.comment: Rejected design direction from c11-c23. The original reporter's gateway configuration already included a resolver, and other affected operators explained that their gateway must issue certificates for some routes while passing other routes to downstream ACME clients. Those affected deployments are folded into the simulated user side without treating their machines as the reporter's machine.

question_patterns: Could you test the developer branch against the same gateway and downstream setup and report what happens?
Please try the candidate build with your existing TCP passthrough configuration and tell me whether downstream challenge traffic works.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I've tested the developer branch, and the passthrough is working like a charm.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I tested the developer branch and downstream TLS challenges still fail exactly as before.
I tested the same developer branch on a second passthrough route and it works there too.

edges.comment: Pre-landing candidate verification from c24. This result came from a different affected operator, not the opening reporter; the affected users are folded into one simulator side, and the answer remains the operator's raw test result.

solution.intent: Use the static per-entry-point AllowACMEByPass option so ACME TLS requests can proceed through normal router matching and reach TLS-passthrough backends, even when the gateway also has its own ACME resolver.
solution.concrete_example: On the relevant TLS entry point, configure `allowACMEByPass: true` (for example under `entryPoints.websecure`). ACME TLS traffic can then match the HostSNI TCP router and pass through to the downstream Traefik instance, while the gateway may retain its own resolver for other routes.

edges.comment: Final technical resolution from c23-c27: maintainers added a static entry-point behavior switch, an affected operator verified the developer branch, and the issue was subsequently closed. The original reporter had separately moved to DNS-01 and did not personally retest the landed implementation.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: affected Traefik gateway versions intercept ACME TLS-ALPN challenges with the internal ACME path before normal TCP router selection, so a TLS-passthrough backend never receives the challenge.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the topology and regression evidence: downstream issuance fails behind the gateway, direct gateway issuance works, and the behavior begins at the rc4 boundary while rc3 works.

Must recommend enabling AllowACMEByPass on the relevant entry point so ACME TLS traffic can follow normal HostSNI router matching to the passthrough backend while the gateway retains its own resolver.
Must not present removing the gateway TLS resolver as the complete solution; affected deployments require gateway-managed ACME and downstream ACME passthrough at the same time.
Must rely on affected-user verification of the candidate behavior, or ask for verification on a build containing the option, before declaring the passthrough problem resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced self-hosting and network operator comfortable with Traefik static and dynamic YAML, TCP SNI routing, TLS passthrough, PROXY protocol, ACME challenge types, and version downgrades.
persona_hint.communication_style: Configuration-heavy and concise; reports concrete version boundaries and topology details, corrects the initial symptom scope, and collaborates with other affected operators on deployment requirements.
